neighbours.label: a noun used as the first half of a compound word, where the next token completes the compound (people|-watch, finger|spell, window|sill, kite|board)
fire: On sunny days we sit outside the cafe and people-watch for hours.
The interpreter had to fingerspell the name of the small town.
She left a pot of herbs on the kitchen windowsill to dry.
He took lessons and learned to kiteboard on the windy beach.
The thieves went dumpster diving for discarded bank statements.
Every winter they go snowboarding in the Alps.
The kids built a sandcastle near the water's edge.
Tariffs are a classic tool of trade protectionism.
quiet: On sunny days we sit outside the cafe and watch the people pass.
The interpreter used her fingers to count the names of the towns.
She opened the kitchen window and left a pot of herbs outside.
He bought a kite and flew it on the windy beach.
The thieves searched the bins for discarded bank statements.
Every winter the snow covers the roads in the Alps.
The kids played in the sand near the water's edge.
Tariffs are a classic tool to protect local industry.
